_readme: The options page, driven by real keys, from both rows a player can press to reach it.
It is in tools/pack_check.sh's list as well as check.sh's, and that is the point of it.
The Window row cycles the palettes in data/palettes/, which are .tres resources that
have to be PACKED - and 'the palettes did not get packed' is a defect every gate running
against res:// is structurally blind to. It is the shape M14 shipped in the audio seam
The sound step is asserted by its CUE rather than by reading a row: the blip is played
after the change so it is heard at the volume just chosen, and it is the only thing a
session can see. The window step is asserted by the state surviving it - a recolour
rebuilds the page it is chosen on, and a rebuild that went wrong would leave no screen.

steps.text: the title, with nothing saved, so the cursor opens on New game. Rows: Continue, New game, Credits, Options - so Options is the LAST row, and two move_ups get there: one onto Continue and one that wraps round the top. Counted up rather than down because wrapping is one deliberate press per row rather than a walk past every row between.
the page is up over the title, with no game behind it - its own flow state, because leaving it goes somewhere different from leaving the one over the world
the cursor opens on Sound. Confirm turns the volume one step and the blip is played AFTER the change, so it is heard at the level just chosen.

down onto Window and change it. The page repaints itself in the colours just chosen, which is the whole point of the row - and a repaint that dropped the screen would fail the state assertion below rather than looking merely wrong.
leave. The title is still behind it and still answers, which is what a screen that latched its answer on the way out would fail.
down onto New game from Options - one press, wrapping the other way - and the run begins
the other way in. Pause, then Options - the LAST row again: Resume, Items, Equipment, Status, Save, Load, Options - so one move_up wraps onto it.

the pause menu CLOSED on the way through, because no overlay here opens over another - so this is the world's options state, not the title's, and leaving goes back to the world rather than to a menu that is already gone.
